info.title: Praxi-Bot daemon API
info.description: Local HTTP API of the bot daemon. Bind: 127.0.0.1 only. Host must be loopback; a browser Origin must be an allowed desktop-app origin; all routes except GET /v1/health and HMAC webhooks need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The disk token has CLI authority only; management, approvals, questions, email configuration and all control/view operations require the desktop per-launch memory-only bearer. Forbidden operations return 403 with migration guidance (ADR-0030).

Explicitly release a latched `paused` / `human_driving`: bots may use the
desktop again.  This is the only way (besides a daemon restart) to end a
pause; heartbeats and a lost app never do.  Idempotent.

get.summary: The daemon's view of the desktop app's controller registration.

put.summary:
Register the desktop app as controller and report its mode (heartbeat: send
it on every state change and at least every 5 s; it expires after 15 s).
While the mode is `human_driving` or `paused`, desktop actions of bots are
refused immediately.  A latched pause is never released by a heartbeat
(`idle` included): send `release: true` with `idle` / `bot_driving` (the
user's resume), or use `POST /v1/control/release`.

post.summary:

overlay highlight) or `refuse` it.

get.summary:
All accounts, with the non-secret fields only (`password_set` says whether

post.summary:
Create an account. The `password` is stored in the secret store (never in
`email.toml`, never returned). `bot` binds the account to one bot (it must
exist); without it every bot that may use the e-mail tools can use it. Takes
effect for the next tool call, no restart needed.

put.summary:
Merge a partial config onto the stored account. Omitted fields keep their
values; `bot: null` makes the account usable by every bot; a `password`
replaces the stored one. Takes effect for the next tool call.

delete.summary:
Remove an account and the secret it owned. Takes effect for the next tool
call. With `delete_inbox=true` the inbox is first deleted at the provider
(irreversible); if that fails the account is kept (`502`) so it can be
retried. Deleting a bot never deletes inboxes at the provider.

parameters.name: delete_inbox
parameters.description:
Also delete the inbox at the provider (`agentmail` accounts). Default
`false`: removing an account only forgets it locally.

422.description: the account has no remote inbox

post.summary:
Try IMAP login and SMTP authentication for a stored account. TLS exactly as
configured; **no mail is sent or read**. A failing server is a normal `200`
with a status per server (`auth_failed`, `tls`, `unreachable`, ...), never
the server's own words. At most two tests run at once (`429`).

Same test for an account that is not saved yet (nothing is stored). With no
`password` in the body, the stored password of the account with the same
`name` is used. Same limits and the same coarse report as the saved test.

get.summary: Documentation stub for the SSE route (the handler lives in `sse.rs`).
get.description:
Server-sent events; each `data:` is a `protocol::Envelope` JSON object, the
SSE `event:` is its `type`.  With `run_id` the SSE `id` is the run-local
`seq` and `Last-Event-ID: <seq>` resumes from the run's NDJSON log.  Without
it the stream covers all runs: the SSE `id` is a daemon-wide, strictly
increasing `gseq` (persisted) and `Last-Event-ID: <gseq>` replays every
missed event of every run, in order, before going live. The desktop UI uses
fetch streaming and Authorization/Last-Event-ID headers. Native `EventSource`
cannot set headers; only this route accepts the low-privilege CLI token in
`token` for legacy clients. Management credentials in query parameters are
rejected. Low-privilege streams omit approval/question decisions; only local
management receives `control_requested`. Filtering applies to live and replay.
Host / Origin checks still apply; query URLs may be logged.

The daemon-wide stream (no `run_id`) also carries `schedule_changed` events
(`dto::ScheduleChanged`: `{"type":"schedule_changed","schedule_id","kind"}`,
kind `created` / `updated` / `toggled` / `deleted`) when a schedule is changed
through the API.  They have no SSE `id`, are not replayed and are not
envelopes: treat them as a hint to refetch `/v1/schedules`.

A replay gap is explicit: `event: gap` has an `id` equal to `to_gseq` and
data `{from_gseq, to_gseq, run_id, reason}`; reason is `log_line_missing` or
`log_unreadable`. It is audited before the cursor passes the missing row.
`/v1/events/status.sse_gaps_total` (authenticated) counts these notifications since daemon startup.
After three consecutive replay failures (or live-buffer overflow),
`event: error` carries `{code: "replay_unavailable", last_event_id}` and the
stream closes. This error has no `id`; reconnect with the last received ID.
Retry delays start at 250 ms and double up to 5 s. Live buffering is limited
to 1000 events and 4 MiB per subscriber; replay chunks hold at most 2 MiB of serialized events (a single larger event closes the stream with `replay_unavailable`), and at most `max_sse_subscribers` streams (default 16) may be open: further requests get `503`. The desktop currently ignores unknown
event names; card 144 can surface gap/error notifications without changing
the ordering or cursor contract.

It likewise carries `mcp_server_changed` events (`mcp::McpServerChanged`:
`{"type":"mcp_server_changed","name","status"}`) when an MCP server is
added, updated, removed or changes status (connecting / connected / error /
quarantined ...); same rules: a hint to refetch `/v1/mcp/servers`.

The newest daemon-wide event cursor (`gseq`, `0` = no event yet): what a
client stores as its resume point after loading a snapshot, so a later
`GET /v1/events` with `Last-Event-ID: <gseq>` replays exactly what came

post.summary:
Add an MCP server, connect it (when enabled) and save `mcp.toml`.  A server
that cannot connect is still added (`status: error`).  Secrets are given as
secret names (`secret_env` / `secret_headers`), never as values; `category`
defaults to `accounts`, `meta` is rejected, `trust_hints` defaults to `false`.

put.summary:
Merge a partial config onto the stored server (it reconnects) and save
`mcp.toml`.  Omitted fields keep their previous values.  `bots: null`
means every bot.  Secret values are never accepted or returned; send
secret **names** in `secret_env` / `secret_headers`.

Reconnect a server (also lifts a quarantine) and refresh its tools.  A
failed connect is reported as `status: error`, not as an HTTP error.

parameters.name: since_ms

post.summary:
Fire a schedule from outside.  No bearer token: the body is authenticated
with `X-Signature-256: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, body)>` (the secret
is the schedule's `webhook_secret`).  Optional replay protection:
`X-Webhook-Timestamp` (Unix ms; then the HMAC must cover `"{timestamp}.{body}"`
and the timestamp must be within 5 minutes) and `X-Delivery-Id` /
`X-GitHub-Delivery` (informational).  A signed request is accepted once per
5-minute window whether or not those headers are sent, so the same body fired
twice in that time needs a timestamp (fresh signature) or a different body.  Host / Origin checks still
apply and the body may be at most 256 KB.  The body replaces `{input}` in the payload.
`202` once accepted (the run goes on in the background).

404.description: no such schedule or no webhook trigger

409.description: disabled, or a run of it is in flight

AcceptedResponse.description:
Answer of `POST /v1/schedules/{id}/run-now` and `POST /v1/webhooks/{id}`:
the run goes on in the background (follow it in the events, with the
`schedule_id` of its `run_started`).

answer.description: The user's answer (free text, or one of the offered options).

call_id.description: Tool call id of the question card.

ApprovalCount.description: Low-privilege status information, without approval IDs or arguments.

ApprovalDto.description: A pending or decided tool-call approval.

tool_name.description: Tool the model wants to call.

oneOf.description:
The truth about what the bot may do: its stored policy merged with its
persisted "always allow" grants.  Only present in `GET /v1/bots/{id}`.

BotInput.description:
Create (`POST /v1/bots`) or replace (`PUT /v1/bots/{id}`) a bot.  Exactly
one of `config` / `profile_toml` is required.

profile_toml.description: Profile as TOML text (the contents of a bot profile file).

key_env.description: Environment variable of the key, for `api_key_env`.

CategoryDecisionDto.description: Effective decision of one permission category.

via_grant.description: `true` when `allow` holds only because of a category grant.

ChannelDto.description: A messaging channel (e.g. Telegram) as seen by the daemon.

enabled.description: The user has not turned the channel off.

running.description: The channel is running inside this daemon.

chat_id.description:
Same as `id`, under the name clients that treat `POST /v1/chats` as
"create chat" expect.

CliAuthState.description: Authentication status reported by a CLI provider (`GET /v1/providers/detected`).

ConfiguredProviderDto.description: A configured provider (never carries a key).

active.description: Loaded in the running loop (a restart or `reload` picks up changes).

custom.description: Not from the catalog: defined by the user.

default_model.description: Chosen default model (without the provider prefix).

has_key.description: A key is stored for it.

models.description: Model ids the provider reports (empty without a listing).

models_error.description: Why the model list could not be fetched.

reason.description: Reason shown to the model on refuse.

ControlMode.description: Who is driving the desktop, as the desktop app's state machine reports it.

ControlStateDto.description: The daemon's view of the controller registration.

app_connected.description: A desktop app is listening on the global event stream.

expires_in_ms.description: Milliseconds until the registration expires; `0` when not registered.

oneOf.description:
`paused` / `human_driving` while latched: refuses bot actions until
`POST /v1/control/release`, regardless of the heartbeat.  `null` when
nothing is latched.

Last reported mode; `null` when no app is registered (never reported,
or the heartbeat expired).

release.description:
With `idle` / `bot_driving`: the user's explicit resume, clears a
latched pause.  Plain heartbeats (without it) never release.

ControlVerdict.description: The app's answer to a `control_requested` event.

reason.description: Reason shown to the model on deny.

scope.description: Scope of an approval (ignored for deny).

DeliveryKind.description: How a sent message was delivered.

account_label.description: Account label (email or org name, max 160 chars, or null).

detail.description: Stable detail code (`not_on_path`, `timeout`, `auth_unparsed`, etc., or null).

installed.description: Whether the CLI binary was found on PATH and `--version` succeeded.

runnable.description: Whether this engine can currently run turns (always false in this task).

version.description: CLI version (first line, trimmed, max 80 chars, or null).

categories.description:
What a human-initiated call of each category resolves to, grants
included (`meta` is always allowed and omitted).

grants.description:
The persisted "always allow" rules.  Tool-level grants only widen that
one tool and are not reflected in `categories`.

policy.description: The profile's own policy as JSON; `null` = the workspace policy applies.

EmailAccountDto.description: A configured account (`GET /v1/email/accounts`): the non-secret fields only.

allowed_senders.description:
Senders whose mail may start a run (stored now, enforced by the inbound
trigger).

bot.description:
Bot (storage UUID) that owns the account; `null` = every bot that may
use the e-mail tools.

custom_ca.description: Whether the account trusts an extra root certificate (a private CA).

imap.description: IMAP server (empty host for API-backed accounts).

inbox_id.description: The provider's id of the inbox (`agentmail` accounts); `null` otherwise.

password_set.description:
Whether the secret (password, or the API key of an `agentmail` account)
is stored. The secret itself is never returned.

allowed_senders.description: Senders whose mail may start a run (addresses or `@domain`).

api_key.description:
The user's own `AgentMail` API key (`agentmail`). **Write-only**: it goes
to the secret store and is never returned or logged.

bot.description: Bot (storage UUID) that owns the account; absent / `null` = every bot.

domain.description:
Custom (verified) domain for a new `agentmail` address; default the
provider's shared domain.

drafts_folder.description: Folder drafts are saved to, default `Drafts`.

name.description:
Account name: 1 to 64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`. Required on
create; for `POST /v1/email/test` it selects the stored password to
reuse when `password` is left out.

name_hint.description: Hint for the local part of a new `agentmail` address.

password.description:
The account password or app password. **Write-only**: it goes to the
secret store and is never returned or logged. Required on create.

provider.description:
Kind of mailbox; default `imap_smtp`. For `agentmail` the inbox is
created at the provider (its address is returned); `address`, `imap`
and `smtp` are not used and `api_key` is required.

EmailAccountPatch.description:
Body of `PUT /v1/email/accounts/{name}`. Every field is optional: a field
left out keeps the stored value. `bot: null` makes the account unbound
(every bot), which is why the handler reads the raw JSON. A `password`
replaces the stored one.

allowed_senders.description: Allowed senders; present list replaces the stored one.

bot.description: Owning bot; `null` = every bot; omit to keep.

EmailProbeStatus.description: What a "test connection" learned about one server.

EmailProviderKind.description: What kind of mailbox an account is.

EmailSecurity.description: How the SMTP connection is secured.

EmailTestReport.description:
Result of a connection test: one status per server, nothing the servers
said.

oneOf.description:
The one API check of an API-backed account (`agentmail`); `imap` and
`smtp` repeat it there. Absent for `imap_smtp`.

ok.description:
Both servers accepted the login (for `agentmail`: the API check
passed).

smtp.description: SMTP (sending mail); authentication only, nothing is sent.

ErrorBody.description: JSON body of an error response.

GrantDto.description: A persisted "always allow" rule of a bot.

oneOf.description: Every tool of a permission category.

status.description: `ok` when ready for inference, or `setup_required` before provider setup.

IsolationStatus.description: Observed daemon isolation state; never contains credentials.

memory_guard_kind.description: Active native guard, or an explicit inactive/unsupported description.

os_sandbox.description: Praxi does not yet provide a full restricted-token/namespace sandbox.

platform.description: OS of the running daemon (not the CLI client).

McpCatalogEntryDto.description: An entry of the curated MCP catalog (`GET /v1/mcp/catalog`).

McpCatalogInstallDto.description:
How to install a catalog entry: send it (plus `name` and `category`) to
`POST /v1/mcp/servers` after storing the `required_secrets`.

McpRequiredSecretDto.description: A secret the user must provide to install a catalog entry.

help_url.description: Where the user can get the value.

McpServerChanged.description:
Data of the `mcp_server_changed` SSE event of the daemon-wide stream: a
server was added, changed, removed, or its status moved.  A notification
only (refetch `/v1/mcp/servers`); no SSE `id`, not replayed, not an envelope.

status.description: New status; `disconnected` for a removed server.

McpServerDto.description:
A configured MCP server (`GET /v1/mcp/servers`).  The full stored config,
except secret *values*: `secret_env` / `secret_headers` carry secret
**names** only.

bots.description: Bots that may use the server; `null` = all bots.

category.description: Permission category of every tool of the server.

enabled.description: Disabled servers are kept but never connected.

tool_allow.description: Glob allow list over server-side tool names; empty = all.

tool_exclude.description: Glob exclude list over server-side tool names.

trust_hints.description: Whether the readOnlyHint annotations of the server are believed.

McpServerInput.description:
Body of `POST /v1/mcp/servers`: the `mcp-bridge` server config.  Secrets go
in `secret_headers` / `secret_env` as secret **names** (store the value with
`POST /v1/secrets/{name}`).

bots.description: Bots that may use the server; absent / `null` = all bots.

category.description: Permission category of the tools; default `accounts`; `meta` is rejected.

name.description:
Server name; `id` is accepted as an alias.  Required on POST; on PUT the
path wins (a different name in the body is rejected).

tool_allow.description: Glob allow list over server-side tool names; empty = all.

tool_exclude.description: Glob exclude list over server-side tool names.

trust_hints.description: Believe the readOnlyHint annotations of the server.  Default `false`.

McpServerPatch.description:
Body of `PUT /v1/mcp/servers/{name}`.  Every field is optional: a field left
out keeps the stored value.  `bots: null` means every bot.  The handler
reads the raw JSON so an omitted field is not the same as `null`.

bots.description: Bots that may use the server.  Omit to keep the list; `null` = all bots.

bots_add.description:
Bot ids to add to `bots`, applied atomically on the stored list (no
read-modify-write by the client).  No effect while the server is open to
every bot (`bots: null`).  Applied after `bots`.

bots_remove.description:
Bot ids to remove from `bots`, applied atomically; an emptied list stays
`[]` (no bot), it never becomes `null`.  Applied after `bots_add`.

category.description: Permission category of the tools; `null` clears it; `meta` is rejected.

enabled.description: Disabled servers are kept but never connected.

env.description: Plain environment variables (stdio).  Present object replaces the map.

headers.description: Plain request headers (http).  Present object replaces the map.

name.description:
Server name; `id` is accepted as an alias.  The path wins (a different
name in the body is rejected).

secret_env.description: Environment variable -> secret name.  Present object replaces the map.

secret_headers.description: HTTP header -> secret name.  Present object replaces the map.

tool_allow.description: Glob allow list over server-side tool names; empty = all.

tool_exclude.description: Glob exclude list over server-side tool names.

oneOf.description: Transport (see [`McpTransportInput`]).  Omit to keep the stored transport.

trust_hints.description: Believe the readOnlyHint annotations of the server.

McpStatus.description: Connection state of an MCP server.

McpToolDto.description: A tool of an MCP server (`GET /v1/mcp/servers/{name}/tools`).

effect.description: `read`, `write` or `destructive` (`destructive` unless the server is trusted).

McpTransportInput.description:
`transport` of an MCP server body: either the kind (`"stdio"` / `"http"`,
with `command` / `args` / `url` as sibling fields, the shape of
[`McpServerDto`]) or the nested `McpServerConfig` object.

McpTransportObject.description: Detailed transport of an MCP server body (the `McpServerConfig` shape).

Mode.description: What to do when the chat already has a running turn.

code.description: The 6-digit code the user sends as `/pair <code>`.

text.description: English or Turkish phrase, e.g. `every weekday at 9`, `her gün 09:00`.

tz.description: IANA timezone for calendar phrases (default UTC).

load_error.description:
Set when the persisted `policy.json` could not be loaded: the daemon is
locked to deny-all until a new policy is saved with `PUT /v1/policy`.

preset.description:
Name of the preset the policy equals (`read-only`,
`approve-destructive`, `read-and-draft`, `full`); `null` = custom.

PolicyInput.description:
`PUT /v1/policy`.  Start from `preset` (or, without it, from the current
policy) and apply the `categories` overrides on top.

active.description: Ids of the providers the running loop can use.

catalog.description: Entries of the built-in provider catalog.

default_provider.description: Id of the loop's default provider.
Id of the new default provider.

route.description:
The route that was cached for the run's request text, tagged by `kind`
(`workflow`, `tool_hint` or `skill_hint`).

can_remember.description:
Whether `POST /v1/runs/{id}/remember` would accept this run (same
checks; nothing is cached by asking).

parent_run_id.description: The run that spawned this one when it is a subagent run.

schedule_id.description: The schedule that started this run (`null` for runs the user started).

ScheduleChanged.description:
Data of the `schedule_changed` SSE event of the daemon-wide stream
(`GET /v1/events` without `run_id`).  It is a notification only (refetch
the schedule): it has no SSE `id`, is not replayed with `Last-Event-ID`
and is not part of `protocol::Envelope`.

chat_id.description:
Chat the runs post to; without one a chat named after the schedule is
used (and created on the first firing).

has_webhook.description:
A webhook trigger is configured (`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}`); the secret
is never returned.

misfire_policy.description:
`skip`, `run_once` or `run_all`: what happens to occurrences missed
while the daemon was down.

next_run_at_ms.description: Next firing (`null` for a disabled or finished schedule).

origin.description:
Who created it: `user`, or `bot` (a bot's schedule tools, after you
approved it). A bot may change only its own `bot` schedules.

bot_id.description: Bot that runs it (cannot be changed afterwards).

chat_id.description: Chat the runs post to (default: a chat named after the schedule).

webhook_secret.description:
HMAC secret of a webhook trigger.  Absent: unchanged (none on create);
the empty string removes the trigger.

mode.description: Behaviour while a turn is running.

run_id.description: The run to follow (`null` when queued: the turn has no run yet).

value.description: The secret value.  Write-only: no route returns it.

SseStatus.description: Counters of the SSE machinery (authenticated, unlike `/v1/health`).

max_sse_subscribers.description: Configured cap on open event streams.

sse_gaps_total.description: Gap notifications emitted by this daemon (per subscriber, since startup).

cost_usd.description:
Cost in USD of the model calls whose price is known; `null` when no
call has a known price.

bearer.description: Low-privilege CLI token stored in `<data dir>/api-token`. Management routes require the separate per-launch memory-only UI bearer; desktop-only locally. The UI bearer is accepted only in Authorization headers, never query parameters.

management.description: Per-launch desktop management credential. Memory and anonymous bootstrap pipe only; never the api-token file. Paired peers authenticate through their transport instead.
